_comment: Static, human-maintained KPI guardrails for cuVSLAM eval, distinct from the rolling
nightly baseline in KPI_HISTORY (which changes every night). cuvslam_kpi_report.py
collect reads this via -b/--baseline_ranges. Nothing here fails the job.
'defaults' applies to every dataset; 'datasets' overrides it per KPI prefix (the
<DATASET> part of a <DATASET>_<METRIC>_<TYPE>_<MODE> key). Settings:
- max_ate_pct, max_lost_frame_pct: a sequence run fails if it tracked no frames,
lost more than max_lost_frame_pct of its frames, has no ATE, or its ATE exceeds
max_ate_pct. Failures are counted in the KPI tables (broken = fails in every
configuration, flaky = in some).
- exclude_failed: also drop failed sequences from the ATE, ARE and Kabsch means;
Losts and FPS always cover every sequence.
- baseline_window, baseline_mad_k, baseline_min_pct: rolling-baseline regression check
against the KPI history. A KPI regresses when it is worse than the median of the
last baseline_window runs by more than max(baseline_mad_k * MAD, baseline_min_pct %
of the median). Only the worse direction counts (FPS down, the rest up); Losts
never flag a change of one lost frame. Needs at least 3 runs of history.
- tolerances: soft drift check against calibrated values, one per metric, 'tol_pct'
(percent of expected) or 'tol_abs' (absolute). A dataset's entry replaces the
default for that metric.
- expected (datasets only): calibrated values keyed <METRIC>_<TYPE>_<MODE>, e.g.
"ATE_MCAM_ODOM": 0.82, or {"value": 0.82, "tol_pct": 5} to override the
tolerance. Uncalibrated KPIs are SKIPPED. Copy steady-state values from a trusted
nightly kpi_<date>.json. The drift check covers the keys the dataset registry says
the suite produces (run_eval.sh passes kpi-keys via -e), so a new dataset needs no
entry here.
